headlines.title: San Jose parents charged with child neglect in fatal asthma death of 8-year-old daughter
headlines.description: A San Jose mother and her husband appeared in court Tuesday to face multiple counts of child neglect in connection with the fatal asthma death of 8-year-old Aurora Williams. Gabrielle Hanson and Jacob Randolph did not enter a plea during their court appearance at the Hall of Justice regarding the May incident. According to court records, Aurora was in medical distress during her asthma attack for at least eight hours before the couple sought medical attention. She later died from a lack of oxygen to the brain, and the medical examiner ruled her death a homicide. When investigators searched the couple’s home, they found six children living in squalor, court documents show. Authorities reported there was no inhaler at the residence and that Aurora’s respirator was unusable because it was filled with cockroaches. “This little girl was filled with roaches, and there was also mold in the home, animal feces, and two parents who were not providing care or food for children,” said Santa Clara County District Attorney Jeff Rosen. Prosecutors have also filed charges against Hanson’s brother, Jonathan Hansen, who was living in the same home. “We are also prosecuting Jonathan Hansen, Aurora’s uncle, and who was living in the same home, for sexually abusing and molesting one of Aurora’s siblings,” Rosen said. In the wake of the case, the district attorney is calling on Santa Clara County to do more to protect children by increasing involvement across multiple agencies. “This is a plan that would create a team of specialists who would work jointly to protect the most vulnerable like Aurora,” Rosen said.

headlines.title: SFUSD commissioners vote on ending school choice lottery in favor of neighborhood models
headlines.description: San Francisco Unified School District commissioners are voting Tuesday night on how to officially end the district’s school choice lottery program, deciding between two options that prioritize keeping students in the neighborhoods where they live. For the last 15 years, families with school-age children in San Francisco have had sometimes stressful starts to each school year because they have to rank their choice of campuses to attend. Parents have complained when schools in their neighborhoods are unavailable or when children in the same family get sent to different campuses. “The lottery is long maligned. No one is in favor of keeping the current lottery, it causes stress for everyone,” said Rebecca Kee, executive director of the San Francisco Parents Coalition. The group recently conducted a survey for feedback on the two options board commissioners will be considering tonight. The first option allows students to attend a school in their neighborhood and includes the option to apply to a school in a different neighborhood if there’s a seat available there. The second also allows students to go to school in their own neighborhood, or they can apply to a different campus, but only if that school has some kind of specialized program. Kee says parents they surveyed preferred the first of those options. “All of these options moving forward are focused on both giving parents a little bit more certainty and peace of mind in the process. But also, the opportunity to have choice and speak up for their child as well,” Kee said. District leaders had been considering three options. In working sessions with parents over the last few months, the superintendent and staff have gone over the details of all of them. “What we are going to do is share with our board and community the tradeoffs that we have to face,” SFUSD Superintendent Maria Su, Ph.D., said during a September 1 session. However, parents in some neighborhoods are raising concerns about what kind of zones will be considered as the district decides what constitutes a neighborhood. Coleman Advocates for Children, which works with Latine, Pacific Islander, and Indigenous families, raised concerns about a possible return to under-resourced schools in certain neighborhoods. A statement from the group reads in part: “Our communities have experienced school assignment policies, desegregation efforts, busing, school choice and other system changes in ways that have not always distributed the benefits or burdens equally.” After tonight’s vote, the details on those neighborhoods will still need to be worked out. The chosen option is expected to be implemented in 2028.

headlines.title: FBI arrests OpenAI employee accused of planting recording device in company office
headlines.description: An engineer at OpenAI has been charged with secretly installing a recording device inside a conference room in what officials said Tuesday was an effort to capture sensitive conversations about the company’s technology. The employee, identified as a 35-year-old Saudi national named Abdulrahman Alfozan, was arrested Friday, a week after the ChatGPT maker discovered an audio recording device hidden inside a company conference room, according to a criminal complaint filed in federal court in San Francisco. The complaint did not identify the company, but the company confirmed in a separate statement that it had discovered a “sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices,” reported the finding to the FBI and fired the employee. “We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier. We referred the matter to the FBI, and we’re grateful to the agents and prosecutors who moved quickly to make an arrest. The FBI’s investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work,” an OpenAI spokesperson said. “At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated,” the statement said. The complaint does not detail what Alfozan might have wanted to do with any captured communications, but the company said the device was sophisticated, designed to evade detection and featured advanced encryption and audio monitoring capabilities. OpenAI said it had evidence the employee planned to place other listening devices throughout other parts of the office building for the purpose of recording meetings. “This alleged attempt by a Saudi national to steal sensitive communications from OpenAI was taken extremely seriously. Theft of intellectual property involving cutting-edge super intelligence technology poses a serious threat to our national security,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement on X. Alfozan made his first court appearance Tuesday on a charge of using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications. It was not immediately clear if he had a lawyer who could speak on his behalf. He is due back in court on Oct. 19. Crime and Courts 14 hours ago Colleges & Universities 11 hours ago Florida 16 hours ago The recording device was found Sept. 30 concealed in toilet paper and inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in an executive conference room, according to the complaint. Though the conference room where the recording device was found did not have a security camera at the time the object was installed, closed-circuit television footage inside the company’s offices revealed that Alfozan was near the conference room on nearly a dozen occasions last month despite not having any authority to access the space or participate in meetings there, the complaint says. The company subsequently added a camera to the room that last week captured Alfozan entering and checking behind the television where the recording device had been installed, according to the FBI. The complaint also alleges that he used a productivity tool to make multiple inquiries about the company’s building addresses, meeting rooms, meeting-room capacities and calendars. Days before his arrest last week, the complaint says, Alfozan left behind an unattended bag in a different room that, when opened by OpenAI personnel, was found to contain his wallet, identification and another recording device similar to the one placed in the conference room.

headlines.title: California Prop 5: What to know about effort to change recall election rules
headlines.description: In November, California voters will decide whether to change the way state leaders can be removed from office. Back in 2021, Gov. Gavin Newsom made a victory speech, decisively defeating a Republican-backed recall effort. “Had it succeeded, his replacement would have been Larry Elder, who would have taken office as governor of the largest state in the union, the fourth largest economy in the world, with only 28% of voter support,” Proposition 5 author Josh Newman said. That’s one of the reasons why Newman said he authored Prop 5: to protect majority rule. Under current rules, voters casting ballots in recall elections face two questions: whether a state elected official should be recalled and who should replace them. Prop 5 would drop the second question to choose a successor, and if the recall passes, a new leader would emerge through an existing process. Newman knows the current process well. The former Democratic state senator was recalled in 2018. “My replacement took office with only 31% of the vote,” he said. “She was, in fact, the person whom I had defeated in 2016 to win in the first place, and then in 2020, I was reelected by a pretty persuasive margin and regained my seat in the state senate.” Newman said the recall process has evolved into a political tool used to seize power. Elections Sep 17 Decision 2026 Oct 2 But critics argue successful efforts have been rare. According to the secretary of state, since 1913, just 11 efforts reached a November ballot. Of those, six were removed from office. “The process is working,” State Senate Minority Leader Brian Jones said. “The people know what they’re doing, the voters know what they’re doing. Let’s just trust the voters and not fix something that’s not broken.” Critics argue Prop 5 would put in place someone who is more of the same, circumventing the process of a recall at all, and add that it would stripe the decision-making power from voters. “To take this power away from the people and put it in place in the supermajority institution is really ridiculous, and the voters should be very cynical about it,” Jones said. It’s unclear how much Prop 5 would cost if passed, but both sides claim the other plan would cost taxpayers more. “You can think about it if it could potentially cost the state more money if the governor or an elected official is recalled and then there has to be a whole separate election to pick a successor rather than having a successor picked on the same ballot,” KQED political correspondent Guy Marzorati said. “Or perhaps it’s a situation where the state ends up saving money, they don’t have to print the materials for that second successor question. Really, I think we’re looking at this measure as not really adding or subtracting from state funds that much.” Marzorati said voters should keep in mind which elected offices would be affected if the proposition passes. “This is just for state elected officials, so we’re talking about statewide constitutional offices, governor, attorney general, secretary of state, and state legislative races, so state senate, state assembly,” he said. “This would not affect all of the recalls that we’ve seen in recent years of district attorneys, of mayors. This would only be for those statewide offices.”

headlines.title: Hispanic Heritage Month spotlight: Chef Nelson German
headlines.description: Nelson German, a Bay Area “Top Chef” who recently was named in Time magazine’s list of 2026 Latino leaders, credits his upbringing and community for his success. Today, German runs three restaurants – two in Oakland and one in San Francisco. He also is a new author and father. NBC Bay Area spoke with German for our latest Hispanic Heritage Month spotlight. Watch the full report in the video player above. headlines.title: Man, 20, allegedly confesses to stabbing coworker to death at San Rafael business
headlines.description: San Rafael police on Monday arrested a 20-year-old man who allegedly confessed to fatally stabbing a coworker over an ongoing dispute. The deadly stabbing happened early Monday afternoon at an undisclosed business in the Northgate One Shopping Center where both the suspect, Justin Amilcar Gutierrez-Navarette of Richmond, and the unidentified victim worked, police said. The two had been tangled up in some sort of dispute before it escalated into a fight and stabbing at the workplace. Officers initially responded shortly after 1 p.m. to the 700 block of Las Gallinas Avenue to investigate a report of an unconscious male who appeared to have fallen, according to police. First responders found a male victim suffering from an apparent stab wound. Authorities later learned the victim exited the rear entrance of the business after being stabbed before he collapsed outside. The victim was rushed to a local hospital, but he did not survive, police said. Detectives launched an investigation and determined the victim, based on his clothing, was an employee at a business in the Northgate One Shopping Center. As authorities were in the beginning stages of the investigation, Gutierrez-Navarette called police and arranged for his surrender. Authorities subsequently interviewed and arrested Gutierrez-Navarette. He was then booked into jail on a charge of murder, police said. The investigation is ongoing. Anyone with information about the case is encouraged to call San Rafael police at 415-485-3000.

headlines.title: WNBA Finals Games 3 and 4 move to State Farm Arena in Atlanta to accommodate more fans
headlines.description: The Atlanta Dream will host the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3 and Game 4 of the WNBA Finals at State Farm Arena, allowing for larger attendance, after the league moved one up a day and altered tipoff of the other to avoid conflicts at the venue. Game 3 of the best-of-seven series will now be Wednesday, Oct. 21. Tipoff for Game 4 on Saturday, Oct. 24 will be 1 p.m. Eastern, 2 1/2 hours before the previously scheduled start time. The series begins Saturday in California. “I put quite a bit of pressure on the commissioner of the NBA and the WNBA. I felt, look, it’s not really about us, it’s about the league,” Warriors and Valkyries owner Joe Lacob said Tuesday in a phone interview with The Associated Press. “The look would not be too good to have Ballhalla and 18,000 fans here and 3,500 over there. I think it’s important for the league to play these games in the finals, a great championship between two very good teams, in front of the same kind of crowd in both places.” The location of the Dream home games had been up in the air because the team wanted to play at State Farm Arena, the home of the Atlanta Hawks that seats more than 17,000 fans, as opposed to their normal home, Gateway Center Arena, which holds only 3,500. The Valkyries have sold out every game in their 18,064-seat Chase Center in San Francisco in their two seasons. “It’s really exciting,” Dream forward Angel Reese said. “I really do enjoy Gateway, so I wouldn’t have minded being here in Gateway. But I know the growth of women’s basketball, the growth of the Atlanta Dream, the support here that we have is just phenomenal and it has continued to skyrocket. “We’re going to miss our Gateway, but I’m really excited to be able to make that happen. Everyone that did make that happen I’m really thankful for it and I’m looking forward to all the fans coming out.” WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert expressed appreciation for the cooperation between the teams and TV networks to make the schedule adjustments. “We are grateful for the efforts made by numerous stakeholders, including the Dream, the Valkyries, the Hawks, State Farm Arena, and NBC Sports and USA Sports,” Engelbert said in a statement. “The change of venue dramatically expands the seating capacity and ensures that the Dream will be able to provide an extraordinary atmosphere for the first WNBA Finals game to be played in the Atlanta market since 2013. We are pleased that thousands more fans across the Southeast region will have the opportunity to experience the ultimate WNBA action — the WNBA Finals — in person.” There were conflicts at State Farm Arena for Game 3, with a concert by singer Sombr on Oct. 22, and for Game 4, with the Hawks holding their home opener the night of Oct. 24. “We are thrilled that we will be able to accommodate the Dream as they host Games 3 and 4 of the WNBA Finals at State Farm Arena. Playing for a championship is special, and we want the Dream to feel the full support of the city during this amazing run,” said Andrew Saltzman, president of business enterprise and chief commercial officer of the Hawks and State Farm Arena. While the Dream played most of their regular-season games at Gateway Center Arena, they moved six regular-season games and the three previous home playoff games to State Farm Arena. They will play all their home games next season at State Farm Arena after signing a multiyear deal earlier this month. It’s unclear where a Game 6 would be held if the WNBA Finals go that long because the Hawks have another home game on Oct. 29. The Valkyries had their own conflict with Game 2 on Oct. 19, when Doja Cat had a concert scheduled that night at Chase Center. The concert was moved to Oct. 25. Gray’s status remains uncertain for the Dream Dream coach Karl Smesko said guard Allisha Gray is improving after missing Game 3 of the semifinal series win over the New York Liberty with a left hand injury. Even so, Smesko said he did not know if Gray, who was a limited participant in Tuesday’s practice, would be available for Saturday’s game. “No word on Game 1,” Smesko said. “But it’s trending in the right direction.” ___ AP Sports Writer Janie McCauley in San Francisco and AP freelance writer Alan Cole in Atlanta contributed to this report. ___ See AP’s full WNBA coverage here

headlines.title: Man fatally struck by cars after leaving disabled vehicle on Highway 101 in San Jose
headlines.description: A motorist who got out of his disabled car along Highway 101 in San Jose over the weekend died after he was hit by vehicles, according to the California Highway Patrol. The collision was reported about 5:30 a.m. Saturday on southbound 101 north of Tully Road. The 36-year-old San Jose man was outside his disabled Toyota on the road when he and his car were hit by a Honda Civic and a Ford, the CHP said. The impact also sent debris into northbound lanes, where it hit a Tesla. The San Jose man, whose name wasn’t released, died at the scene. The driver of the Honda suffered major injuries and was transported to a hospital. The Ford’s driver wasn’t injured and the Tesla driver had minor injuries. The three drivers weren’t driving under the influence, the CHP said. Any witnesses or persons with information about this crash are asked to contact the San Jose CHP Area Office at 408-961-0900.

headlines.title: CHP arrests suspect in connection with Bay Bridge freeway shooting
headlines.description: A California Highway Patrol investigation has identified two suspects and led to the arrest of one in connection with a freeway shooting that injured a passenger, authorities announced Monday. On Sept. 26, CHP officers responded to a shooting on eastbound Interstate 80 west of the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge toll plaza, according to the agency. Investigators determined the shooting appeared targeted and retaliatory, stemming from an earlier physical altercation in San Francisco. According to authorities, the suspects allegedly followed the victims onto the freeway after the altercation and opened fire on their vehicle, striking a passenger in the leg. Investigators with the CHP Golden Gate Division Major Crimes Unit identified the suspects as 19-year-old Olman Santiago Martinezaguilar of San Pablo and a 15-year-old boy from Richmond. At about 6:15 a.m. Oct. 8, the CHP Golden Gate Division Warrant Service Team executed search and arrest warrants at residences in Richmond and San Pablo. Officers arrested Martinezaguilar at his San Pablo residence and recovered a firearm they believe is associated with him. The juvenile suspect was already in custody on an unrelated matter. Authorities booked Martinezaguilar into Santa Rita Jail on charges related to attempted murder, shooting at an occupied vehicle, and other offenses. “As California’s state police, the CHP is committed to protecting the public and holding people accountable for violence that endangers our communities,” said CHP Golden Gate Division Chief Steve Ramos. “This arrest reflects our investigators’ dedication to identifying those responsible and keeping Californians safe.”

headlines.title: Jury selected in corruption trial of former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao
headlines.description: After a full day of questioning, a jury was selected Tuesday for the corruption trial of former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao. The jury is made up of seven women and five men, representing different races, age groups and counties. The final selection came after the defense struck 15 potential jurors, while the prosecution dismissed eight. Opening statements are slated to begin Wednesday. Federal prosecutors indicted Thao on charges of bribery, conspiracy and wire fraud, along with her longtime boyfriend Andre Jones and David and Andy Duong. The Duongs own California Waste Solutions – Oakland’s recycling contractor – and a modular home company. “The jury selection process can be tedious, but it’s vital to both sides,” legal analyst Steven Clark said. “If you don’t do a good job in jury selection as an attorney, you can lose your case before it starts.” Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers asked whether potential jurors could remain fair and impartial if a defendant chooses not to testify. “The judge is trying to ensure that if someone does take the Fifth, it doesn’t mean they’re guilty of anything and it’s a legal right they have to do,” Clark said. “So what the judge is trying to do is foretell the type of case they’re going to be hearing in this jury.” Gonzalez Rogers also asked whether potential jurors have any biases involving law enforcement, gender, religion or race. Thao and the Duongs are Asian American. Jones is African American. Prospective jurors raised concerns about scheduling, political biases and negative experiences with law enforcement. One potential juror said she’s a civil prosecutor herself. After the judge questioned them, attorneys from both sides got to grill the prospective jurors. “You want to try to get as much information about these jurors because you do have the right to excuse some of them, and you want to use those choices wisely,” Clark said. Defense attorneys asked whether Thao’s recall from office could affect their impartiality and if they could evaluate each defendant individually. Clark said Thao’s public profile could make that challenging. “She has a difficult time coming into this case with a clean slate, particularly with people that may have been affected by her conduct who live in Oakland,” Clark said. “I think what the defense wants to do is have a wide array of jurors who don’t bring that in, that institutional knowledge of this case, with them.” Sheng Thao Sep 23 Sheng Thao Sep 4 Sheng Thao Aug 14 Federal prosecutors charge Thao and her co-defendants with bribery, conspiracy and fraud. Prosecutors allege Thao helped the Duongs’ companies secure future city contracts in exchange for election support and payments to Jones. All four defendants have pleaded not guilty. If convicted, they could face up to 20 years in prison on the most serious charges. Recently released phone recordings include one from 2019 indicating Thao discussed concerns that the recycling company overcharged the city. Court records also include a transcript from a 2024 phone call between Andy Duong and an unnamed Oakland city councilmember. Early in the conversation, Duong invites the councilmember to “party up in the yacht” and, in the future, “a private [yacht] for us only,” according to the transcript. When the councilmember asks about the recall effort against then-Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao, Duong says, “We put a stop to it.” Thao was eventually recalled later that year.

headlines.title: Motorcyclist killed in crash on westbound I-80 in Emeryville
headlines.description: A motorcyclist died in a crash on westbound Interstate Highway 80 in Emeryville near the MacArthur Maze on Tuesday morning, according to the California Highway Patrol. The crash was reported shortly after 6:45 a.m. on westbound I-80 west of Powell Street. The motorcyclist died in the crash, which was still blocking traffic on the highway an hour later. No other details about the case were immediately available from the CHP.

headlines.title: Bay Area voter guide: What to know about the November 2026 election
headlines.description: What to Know — Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026 California will choose a new governor to replace Gavin Newsom, who terms out after this year. The choices are Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton. Voters will decide 14 state propositions. Regional sales tax Measure RTM, the Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, aims to increase funds for public transit. California’s Congressional District 11 race features Scott Wiener and Connie Chan competing to succeed Nancy Pelosi. Aisha Wahab and Melissa Hernandez will face off again after a special election in August where Wahab secured victory to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. All 80 California Assembly seats are up for reelection, as well as 20 Senate seats. California’s general election is Nov. 3, with statewide races and propositions as well as key local races and measures across the Bay Area. Here’s what you need to know to cast your ballot, including important dates and deadlines, how to register or check your status, where and when to vote, and what’s on the ballot. In this guide: Key election dates Check voter registration status How to register to vote How to find your polling place What to bring to your polling place How to track your mail-in ballot Why is California choosing a new governor? 14 California propositions What to watch Alameda County What to watch Contra Costa County What to watch Napa County What to watch San Francisco What to watch San Mateo County What to watch Santa Clara County What to watch Solano County County election offices Key election dates The last day to register to vote for the Nov. 3 general election is Oct. 19. County election officials will start mailing ballots by Oct. 5. Ballot drop-off locations open on Oct. 6 Last day to register to vote for the general election is Oct. 19. First vote centers open for early in-person voting in all Voter’s Choice Act counties on Oct. 24. In person early voting locations in the state open on Oct. 31. Election Day, Nov. 3, is the last day to vote in-person or return a ballot by 8 p.m. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Vote-by-mail ballots must be postmarked no later than Nov. 3. If mailing on election day, get a hand-stamped postmark from a postal employee inside a post office. Visit the California Secretary of State’s website for a full list of key dates and deadlines. Check voter registration status Voters can check their registration at voterstatus.sos.ca.gov to confirm their mailing address and voting status. How to register to vote California residents can register to vote in elections at registertovote.ca.gov. Note Oct. 19 is the last day to register for the general election. Same day voter registration window will be open from Oct. 20 up to the Nov. 3 election day. Visit caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov for a list of early voting locations to complete same day registration. How to find your polling place Visit the California Secretary of State’s website, where you can input your address to find your polling location and see what is on your ballot. Voters can also visit their county elections office for more information. Scroll down to the Bay Area county election offices section of this guide for further contact information. What to bring to your polling place Voters usually are not required to show identification to a polling place worker before casting a ballot, according to the Secretary of State’s website. There are some instances when providing identification is required: Voting for the first time after registering to vote by mail and did not provide a driver license number California identification number or the last four digits of social security number are missing on registration form In these cases voters should plan to bring identification to a polling place or bring a copy of it with their vote-by-mail ballot. The Secretary of State says the following are acceptable forms of identification: Passport Driver license Official state identification card Student identification card Copy of recent utility bill Sample ballot booklet received from county elections office Any document received by a government agency How to track your mail-in ballot Voters can track their vote-by-mail ballot and confirm it has been received by using the state’s Where’s My Ballot? tool at california.ballottrax.net/voter/. Ballots mailed in may take a few days to appear on the website. Why is California choosing a new governor? Gov. Gavin Newsom terms out after this year and voters will choose between Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton, who both advanced to the general election after a wild primary. Becerra has served as former President Joe Biden’s top health official and oversaw the response to the coronavirus pandemic. He was also the California’s attorney general during President Donald Trump’s first term and has more than two decades of experience as a congressmember. Hilton was a conservative commentator with a show on Fox News for six years. He also worked as an adviser to former British prime minister David Cameron. What are the 14 California propositions voters will decide in the November election? Here’s a list of the California propositions on the November ballot. Use the expandable graphic below for a breakdown on what to know about each measure. 2026 California Ballot Propositions Click on a proposition to see more information about what will happen if it does or doesn’t pass. Source: NBC Staff Reports • Interactive: Annetta Stogniew Regional measure to watch Measure RTM: The Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, is a regional sales tax aimed at increasing funds for public transit. It includes 5 Bay Area counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara. Races and measures to watch in Alameda County California Congressional District 14: California lawmaker Aisha Wahab and Bay Area Rapid Transit Director Melissa Hernandez will face off again to determine who will serve the next full two-year term. Wahab topped Hernandez in an August special election to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. Swalwell resigned from Congress earlier this year after sexual assault and misconduct allegations. District 14 includes the East Bay cities such as Fremont, Hayward and Livermore. Measure X in Berkeley: Would establish 10% limit on annual rent increases and other changes to the city’s rent ordinance. Measure Y in Berkeley: Parcel tax to pay for arts projects. Measure Z in Berkeley: Parcel tax to fund a public bank. Measure AA in Berkeley: Increase soda tax (not assigned) Measure EE in Oakland: Shift city to a strong mayor system. Measure FF in Oakland: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Alameda County and additional election information, visit the Alameda County Elections website. In Richmond, residents will vote on a new mayor while voters in San Pablo will weigh in on Measure S, which would limit rent increases. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Contra Costa County and additional election information, visit the Contra Costa County Elections website. Proposition A: Give mayor more power to hire and fire department heads. Proposition B: Pave way for public bank. Proposition C: Increase the city’s annual contribution to an affordable housing trust fund. Proposition D: New barriers to placing measures on the ballot. Proposition E: Changes to city contracting. Proposition G: Reopen parts of the Great Highway to vehicle traffic on weekdays. Proposition H: Parcel tax to fund Muni. Proposition J: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax California Congressional District 11: Scott Wiener and Connie Chan compete to succeed Nancy Pelosi. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Francisco and additional election information, visit the San Francisco Department of Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Mateo County Measure E in Redwood City: Limit rent increases. Measure Q in Half Moon Bay: Referendum to block proposed farmworker housing. Measure U in San Mateo County: Create independent commission to draw supervisor districts. For a complete list of San Mateo County measures and races on the ballot, visit smacre.gov/elections. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Mateo County and additional election information, visit the San Mateo County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Santa Clara County In San Jose, incumbents Peter Ortiz and Bien Doan are up for re-election in Districts 5 and 7, respectively, and there’s an open seat in District 9. Races and measures to watch in Solano County Solano County Board of Supervisors, District 4: Mike Silva and John Carli face in a runoff in a district covering Vacaville and Dixon. Measure E in Solano County: New tax on data centers and battery storage facilities in the unincorporated county areas. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Solano County and additional election information, visit the Solano County Registrar of Voters website.
